description: Reference choreography from the @avyns.draft TikTok (22.4 s of dance before the end card). Solo dancer framed waist up: hand and arm gestures only. Move boundaries from the wrist/elbow trajectories and motion energy of data/dance/pose/avyns_draft_979019.npz (see docs/DANCE_MODEL_INTERFACE.md section 4 for the schema).

moves.name: Ready: step back from the phone and stand with arms down
Hands clasp together and press to the screen-right cheek, then to the screen-left cheek
Hands drop to the waist and roll from screen-right to screen-left, then small gestures in front of the chest: open palm lifts, hands tap and fold
Lean in close to the camera with a fist at the chin, then both open palms beckon beside the face while stepping back
Screen-left fist pumps beside the head while the other arm hangs, then the hands fold together at the chest
Both hands pump up to the shoulders and down to the hips twice, then the arms raise alternately beside the head
A hand sweeps forward to cover the camera, twice, returning to the shoulders in between
Fists pump up beside the shoulders and down with a bounce, then the screen-right arm rises high and waves
A hand covers the camera, both hands lift beside the face, a hand covers it again, then both arms wave overhead

notes: Knees are visible in under 10% of frames and ankles never: the 'legs' fault never fires on this dance.

'ready' is the count-in: the dancer steps back from the phone during 0-0.8 s and then stands with arms down; the judge's reference clock starts count_in_s after the first ok learner frame unless set_ref_clock is used.

Short tracking gaps (ok=False) at 15.63-15.67 s, 19.27 s and 19.33 s are the hand covering the lens; the end card starts at 22.77 s. Hips are NaN from about 22.4 s as the dancer lunges at the phone to stop recording, so the last move ends at 22.4 s.
Hand pumps repeat every ~0.6-0.65 s (11.5-12.6 s and 16.4-17.9 s) but the periodicity is weak and short; bpm left null.
Several moves are hand-shape gestures (clasped hands, open palm, thumbs-up fist) that COCO-17 wrists only partially capture; the judge mainly sees wrist height and side.
